title: Caps punch statements to an accent name reveal
summary: One line on black, a cut to light grey, then half-sentences built word by word that each land on a single uppercase punch word. An eyebrow and an accent-coloured name reveal follow, three short claims, and a wordmark with a tagline close.
use_when: A problem-to-promise story told with type only, before any UI is worth showing
Silent autoplay where each sentence must split into a setup and a one-word payoff
Naming a product with one accent colour on an otherwise neutral light film
A 15-20 s teaser for a simple tool with three verb claims

sfx.event: hard cut from the black opening to the light background
product name resolves in the accent colour under the eyebrow

params.brand: any brand.json: display font, fg, muted, accent (product name), bg; the opening uses black bg + white text
params.content.hook: opening setup line on black, 2-3 words with an ellipsis
params.content.pairs: 3 setup + punch pairs: setup half-sentence 2-5 words, punch = one uppercase word that completes it
params.content.eyebrow: tiny uppercase label before the name, e.g. 'Introducing'
params.content.name: product name, shown once in the accent colour and once as the dark closing wordmark with a period
params.content.claims: 3 claims, 2-3 words each, verb first, ending in a period
params.content.tagline: small closing line under the wordmark, 3 short words

notes: Studied from 4 fps sheets (±0.25 s): no 30 fps strips were made because the analysis dir is read-only. The reference is silent (no music, no VO), so sfx are planned by the glue rule, not measured. Setup lines are laid out at their final centred position and fill word by word, so they never re-centre. Punch words are uppercase and always alone on screen; they follow their setup line with no empty frame, and the third (row 8) blur-crossfades over it. The only hard cut is black to light at 1.13 s. Camera creep is 0.5-2.6 %/s from motion.json, never fully static. Proposed terms (not used as ids): caps-punch, mask-sink.
